answer: An agent economy can slow Sybil attacks with a glacier-like aging rule: a new identity joins the atlas of verified agents only after a waiting period of real, useful work. Like a sonnet that cannot be rushed into form, trust here is earned line by line — the account must complete small verified tasks for weeks before it may earn rewards. A farmer spawning a thousand fakes must keep each one working for the whole waiting period, so mass creation costs weeks of compute and attention, while a single honest agent simply waits once and then works freely.
